comment: The offline-capability requirement is useful, but “central platform” unnecessarily prescribes a topology that conflicts with the Guidance's otherwise stated support for centralised, federated and hybrid implementation. Surveillance in decentralised systems may involve regional operational nodes synchronising with national coordination infrastructure without one central platform functioning as the sole operational data store. The requirement concerns reliable synchronisation and continuity, not architectural centralisation, and should therefore remain topology-neutral

public.text: The offline-capability requirement is useful, but “central platform” unnecessarily prescribes a topology that conflicts with the Guidance's otherwise stated support for centralised, federated and hybrid implementation. Surveillance in decentralised systems may involve regional operational nodes synchronising with national coordination infrastructure without one central platform functioning as the sole operational data store. The requirement concerns reliable synchronisation and continuity, not architectural centralisation, and should therefore remain topology-neutral
public.suggestedRevision: Replace “the central platform” with “the designated surveillance platform or authorised synchronisation endpoint(s), which may be centralised, federated or hybrid according to the jurisdiction's architecture.”
